6 تبازخ He walked, or sat, in the manner of him who is termed أَبْزَخ. (L.) And تبازخت She (a woman) made her posteriors to stick out: (S:) or she had prominent posteriors: (K:) or she (an old woman, in walking,) erected her backbone, and made the part between her shoulders to recede, and bent the part above it, next her neck: (L:) or she had her posteriors prominent, and the upper part of her back, next the neck, bent. (TA.) ―
-b2- He (a horse) bent his hoof towards his belly, because of the shortness of his neck, at the time of drinking. (TA.) ―
-b3- تبازخ عَنِ الأَمْرِ (tropical:) He drew back, held back, or hung back, from the thing, or affair; would not go forward in it. (S, A, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
